events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Relative humidity will fall below 25 percent for much of the
afternoon. Given the dry vegetation and low fine fuel moisture,
outdoor fires will be able to spread quickly once started,
increasing the danger of wildfires.

Please refer to your local burn permitting authority on whether
you can burn today. If you do burn, use extreme caution since
fires can quickly get out of hand under these conditions.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Northwest Plateau
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Arizona, including the following
area, Northwest Plateau.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms are expected to
impact portions of northern Mohave County Wednesday morning
through Thursday. A heavy rain and flash flood threat may develop
in areas experiencing repeated rounds of storms.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
